miniProject.title: Portability audit with a clean reproduction and a losing regime
miniProject.brief: Close the track as defensible engineering on your GPU: a peak table with named clocks, an AMD dispatch defense, a tested fallback gate and a repaired misleading benchmark. Reconstruct one production path, rebuild clean, and file a workload-weighted report that keeps a loss. Build with `-arch=native` and size all work to fit your GPU's memory.
steps: Build a per-kernel peak table that names its clock source, place each kernel against its ridge point, and file the regime prediction with the falsifier that would reject it.

Write the dispatch defense so each path names its AMD CDNA and HIP counterpart. Test all three fallback branches on your GPU: native, forced portable fallback, and the explicit error below the portable minimum. Hopper and Blackwell paths your GPU lacks stay static audit.

Fix the stack for the full shape matrix, reporting boundaries, precision, distributions, held-out status and frequency per shape. Audit one deliberately misleading benchmark against timing boundary, baseline parity, distributions, held-out status and cherry-picking, and correct every flaw with matched precision shown.

Run one KernelBench Level 1 problem in your harness, add one negated test that a reward-hacked kernel fails, and derive the SOL-ExecBench bound by hand for one row. List what each held-out axis would break; treat paths your GPU cannot run as reading only.

Trace one production kernel through graph, IR, dispatch and profile with bytes, launches and resources at each link. Write one bounded change with a predeclared mechanism and the profiler signal that would falsify it, tested on unseen shapes.

Regenerate the full shape matrix from a clean checkout with raw samples and claim-to-artifact links for every table entry. Exercise every protection with an injected-defect test it catches, for example an unsupported dtype reaching the fast path.

Build the workload-weighted table with one losing row kept, and write the three-question defense: a stronger baseline, an alternate explanation, and the maintenance cost. State the dispatch choice per kernel family from the clean reproduction.
deliverables: The peak-bound table with named clocks and ridge points, and the AMD dispatch defense with fallback tests.
The scenario-fixed shape matrix, the repaired misleading benchmark, and the KernelBench plus SOL notes.
The reconstructed path with its bounded change, the clean-build regeneration, and the weighted report with a loss.

rubric.pass: Peaks name clocks with ridges derived, each path names its AMD counterpart in your own tests, and all three fallback branches pass.
rubric.strong: The table states which Hopper and Blackwell features remain static audit.

rubric.pass: The shape matrix fixes the stack with boundaries and frequency stated, the misleading benchmark is repaired on all five lines with matched precision, and paths your GPU cannot run are marked reading only.
rubric.strong: Held-out shapes and values are named with what each would break.

rubric.pass: The clean checkout regenerates tables with raw samples and claim links, each protection has an injected-defect test, and the weighted report keeps a losing row with its defense.
rubric.strong: The per-family dispatch choice names its maintenance cost.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone defense: the peak table, audit, reconstruction, clean reproduction and weighted report with the losing regime are the final evidence package.
